links.outcome: Model versus physician mTICI agreement under report-only, images-only, and combined input conditions
links.effect: GPT-5 matched readers with report (wκ 0.87 vs 0.87) but fell to wκ 0.35 on images only (readers 0.85); MedGemma-1.5 wκ 0.34, 0.34, 0.02.
links.quote: Multimodal frontier models can achieve physician-level mTICI agreement when procedural reports are available, but performance drops substantially on images alone.

links.outcome: AI mTICI grading compared with physician readers on same cases
links.effect: GPT-5 was comparable to pooled readers with a report (wκ 0.87 vs 0.87) but far worse on images alone (0.35 vs 0.85); MedGemma-1.5 performed poorly throughout.
links.quote: GPT-5 was virtually indistinguishable from pooled readers when a report was available (images plus report wκ 0.87 [95% confidence interval: 0.78, 0.92]; report only 0.86 [0.78, 0.92]; readers 0.87 [0.81, 0.91] for both), but image-only agreement collapsed to wκ 0.35 [0.08, 0.56] (readers 0.85 [0.78, 0.90]).

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic/assessment accuracy of multimodal models (GPT-5, MedGemma-1.5) compared to clinicians across different input modalities on a retrospective dataset, without evaluating a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
